originalText:
Misbegotten

By day, the lands around the Occlusion are empty,
the wreckage of the terrain left in ruin by some
forgotten calamity. By night, the blasted expanse
comes to life, when the misbegotten crawl out
from the rocks, from beneath the shelves, and out
of the pits pocking the surface, liberated by the
sun’s departure and ready to feed their vile appetites
for food and pleasure.
The misbegotten are a breed of monster created
by the cabalists’ failed experiments. Cast out from
the Occlusion, the misbegotten must make do in the
wild. Formed from human stock, the misbegotten still
show some signs of their heritage, being humanoid in
shape, but always marked in some way or another by
the horrors inflicted on them. Abraded flesh, hideous
scars, extra appendages, misshapen features, and
worse beset them, but in no way diminishes their
hunger or their desire to copulate.
The misbegotten range far from the Occlusion
each night, scouring the lands for anything they
might eat or fuck. Often, they fall on their victims,
devouring them and violating their corpses, spilling
their purplish seed into wounds left by their claws
and teeth. When forced to go without, they howl in
fury and turn on each other in an orgy of violence. In
no danger of running out of their kind, such is their
fecundity, the appalling slaughter serves to keep their
numbers in check.

MISBEGOTTEN

DIFFICULTY 25

Size 1 frightening monster
Perception 15 (+5); darksight
Defense 14; Health 30; Insanity —; Corruption 1d6 + 6
Strength 13 (+3), Agility 14 (+4), Intellect 8 (–2), Will 15 (+5)
Speed 12
Immune charmed, dazed, slowed
Stench of the Living The misbegotten knows the location
of each living creature within medium range. Such
creatures cannot become hidden from the misbegotten.
Sunlight Weakness A misbegotten is impaired while in
areas lit by sunlight.

ATTACK OPTIONS
Claws and Teeth (melee) +3 with 3 boons (3d6 plus Overpower)
Overpower If the target is a creature of the misbegotten’s
Size or smaller, the target must get a success on a
Strength challenge roll or fall prone.

SPECIAL ACTIONS
Unchecked Aggression When a creature within medium
range of the misbegotten would take a fast turn and
the misbegotten is hostile to it, the misbegotten can
use a triggered action to move up to its Speed toward
the triggering creature. If the misbegotten can reach
the triggering creature at the end of this movement, it
imposes 1 bane on the creature’s attack rolls until the
end of the round.

MISBEGOTTEN MOB

DIFFICULTY 100

Size 3 frightening monster
Perception 15 (+5); darksight
Defense 14; Health 120; Insanity —; Corruption 1d6 + 6
Strength 13 (+3), Agility 14 (+4), Intellect 8 (–2), Will 15 (+5)
Speed 12
Immune charmed, dazed, slowed
Mob A mob takes half damage from attacks that target
individual creatures and double damage from attacks
that affect an area. The mob acts as a single creature,
but it counts as ten creatures for the purpose of choosing
targets. A mob makes Strength, Intellect, and Will
challenge rolls with 1 boon.
Creatures can move through a mob’s space, but must
treat the area as difficult terrain. The mob can squeeze
through openings large enough to permit the passage
of an individual member and can move through space
occupied by other creatures.
Spawn When the mob becomes incapacitated, it dissipates
and 1d6 misbegotten appear in open spaces within the
space the mob formerly occupied. These creatures can
take the next available turn.
Stench of the Living The misbegotten mob knows the
location of each living creature within medium range. Such
creatures cannot become hidden from the misbegotten.
Sunlight Weakness A misbegotten mob is impaired while
in areas lit by sunlight.

ATTACK OPTIONS
Claws and Teeth (melee) +3 with 5 boons (5d6 plus
Overpower or 3d6 plus Overpower if the mob is injured)
Overpower If the target is a creature of the misbegotten
mob’s Size or smaller, the target must get a success on
a Strength challenge roll or fall prone.

SPECIAL ACTIONS
Overwhelm If the mob is not injured, each creature that
isn’t a swarm or a mob that is inside the mob’s space
or within 1 yard of it must get a success on an Agility
challenge roll or take 2d6 damage.
Unchecked Aggression When a creature within medium
range of the misbegotten mob would take a fast
turn and the mob is hostile to it, the mob can use a
triggered action to move up to its Speed toward the
triggering creature. If the misbegotten mob can reach
the triggering creature at the end of this movement, it
imposes 1 bane on the creature’s attack rolls until the
end of the round.

name: CABALIST OF THE BLACK SUN

originalText:
CABALIST OF THE BLACK SUN DIFFICULTY 250
Size 1 horrifying human
Perception 16 (+6); darksight
Defense 17 (arcane retribution); Health 50; Insanity 1d6 + 4;
Corruption 9
Strength 11 (+1), Agility 12 (+2), Intellect 16 (+6), Will 15 (+5)
Speed 10
Immune frightened
Spell Defense The cabalist takes half damage from spells.
When a creature casts an attack spell at the disciple, the
cabalist imposes 1 bane on the attack roll and makes the
challenge roll to resist the spell with 1 boon.
Unbound Movement The cabalist can walk across the air
as easily as it can walk across the ground. A cabalist
moving in the air can remain there, without falling.
Wind from the Outer Dark When the cabalist casts a spell,
a fetid wind whirls around it until the end of the round.
The wind disperses smoke, fog, vapor, and mist within
5 yards of the cabalist and imposes 1 bane on attack rolls
made against the disciple using ranged weapons.

ATTACK OPTIONS

Black Sun Singer

As the sun slips behind the horizon and long shadows
stretch across the ground, reaching toward the
Occlusion, the Black Sun singers emerge from the
black recesses to lift their voices up in song to the
alien gods. Vaguely human, horrific scars covering
their faces and the mutilation of their mouths and
ears offer clues about the torments to which they had
been subjected. Singers lack ears, the flesh burned
away with hot irons and the holes covered over with
scar tissue. Their mouths hang open, stretching
impossibly wide whenever they sing, and their eyes,
yellow and bleary, roll about in their heads.
Black Sun singers gabble incoherently and, lacking
ears, cannot understand anything said to them.

BLACK SUN SINGER
Size 1 monster

Perception 6 (–4); shadowsight
Defense 11; Health 18; Insanity —; Corruption 1
Strength 9 (–1), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 8 (–2), Will 9 (–1)
Speed 6
Deafened Black Sun singers are deafened.
Screeching Death When a Black Sun singer becomes
incapacitated, it screeches, forcing each creature within
short range that can hear the noise to make a Will
challenge roll. On a failure, the creature gains 1 Insanity.

Blade (melee) +2 with 1 boon (1d6)

ATTACK OPTIONS

SPECIAL ATTACKS

Fists (melee) +1 (1d3)

Horrid Tendrils The cabalist flings twisting purple ribbons
of light at up to three creatures it can see within medium
range, making an Intellect attack roll with 2 boons against
the Agility of each target. On a success, the ribbons hit
the target, burning it for 6d6 damage, and moving the
target up to 5 yards in any direction. If the total of the
attack roll is 20 or higher and beats the target number
by 5 or more, the target takes 2d6 extra damage and
becomes dazed for 1 minute. A target dazed in this way
can make a Will challenge roll at the end of each round,
removing the affliction from itself on a success.

SPECIAL ACTIONS
Aid from the Alien Dark When the cabalist gets a failure
on an attack roll or challenge roll, it can use a triggered
action to turn the failure into a success. The cabalist then
gains 1 Insanity and takes 1d6 damage.
Pierce the Flickering Veil When a creature makes an attack
roll against the cabalist, the cabalist can use a triggered
action to teleport to an open space within medium range.

MAGIC
Power 5
Arcana arcane armor (5), magic dart (6), arcane shield (3),
unerring darts (3), explosive darts (2), arcane lightning (2),
harness magic (1), arcane retribution (0; already cast)
Curse hex (6), pox (6), hobble (3), pain (3), vulnerability (2),
weakness (2), dread (2), toad (1), petrify (1)

END OF THE ROUND
Epic Recovery The cabalist removes one affliction from
himself.

DIFFICULTY 5

SPECIAL ATTACKS
Song of the Outer Gods The Black Sun singer uses an
action to sing the song of the Outer Gods and continues
to sing for as long as it concentrates. When the singer
starts to sing and, again, at the end of each round it
spent singing, each creature within medium range of at
least one singing singer and that can hear the song must
make a Will challenge roll. For each singing singer within
medium range after the first, the creature makes the roll
with 1 bane. On a failure, the target gains 1 Insanity. On
a success, the creature becomes immune to the Song of
the Outer Gods until after it completes a rest.
Sonic Dissonance The Black Sun singer creates a
disharmonic noise that ruptures flesh and shatters
objects inside a 3-yard-cone originating from a point in
its space. Each creature and object in the area takes 2d6
damage from the sound. A creature can make a Strength
challenge roll and takes half the damage on a success.

Idiotic Crooners

The Black Sun singers perform their unsettling
music out of some obligation imprinted on them by
their masters. They show little regard for their own
safety let alone for their surroundings, which they
generally ignore. The true danger they pose, however,
comes from their song, and people who hear their
awful chorus tumble into madness as they envision
impossible vistas and mountain-sized gods drifting in
the gulfs of space.

11

originalText:
Crung

As accomplished as the cabalists are in the use of
magic, their numbers are too few to adequately
protect themselves from their enemies. For
this reason, they made the crung to serve as
their soldiers and guards, and charged them with
destroying anyone who would dare breach the
sanctity of the Occlusion. Once humans, the crung
have been pumped with so many chemicals their
bodies bulge, bones grown to weird length, features
all twisted up into leering grins. Crung stand 9 feet
tall and weigh several hundred pounds.
Crung do not speak, but they understand the
Common Tongue.

Lumbering Guardians

CRUNG

DIFFICULTY 50

Size 2 frightening monster
Perception 10 (+0); darksight
Defense 9; Health 80; Insanity —; Corruption 3
Strength 15 (+5), Agility 9 (–1), Intellect 8 (–2), Will 11 (+1)
Speed 12
Immune charmed, frightened
Explosive Rage When the crung becomes injured and is
capable of using actions, each creature within 1 yard of
it must get a success on an Agility challenge roll or take
1d6 damage from its flailing limbs. Until the crung is no
longer injured, it makes attack rolls with 1 bane, but its
melee attacks deal 1d6 extra damage.

ATTACK OPTIONS
Cleaver (melee) +5 with 2 boons (3d6 plus Brutality on
attack roll 20+)
Rock (medium range) +5 with 1 boon (2d6)
Brutality The target takes 3d6 extra damage and must get
a success on a Strength challenge roll with 1 bane or fall
prone.

SPECIAL ATTACKS
Murderous Strike If the crung can reach two or more
creatures, it can use an action to make a cleaver attack.
It compares the result of its attack roll to the Defense of
each creature it chooses within its reach. On a success,
the creature takes damage from the cleaver attack.

SPECIAL ACTIONS

12

Unchecked Aggression When a creature moves to a space
inside the crung’s reach, the crung can use a triggered
action to use its cleaver to attack the triggering creature.

Crung guard entrances into the Occlusion, usually
standing in shadowed alcoves where they can’t be
immediately seen. If the player characters venture
into the stronghold, they might encounter up to five
of these brutes, who lurch out of their hiding places
to chop up the intruders. Crung demonstrate
their single-mindedness in combat, focusing
their attacks against the nearest foe. However,
if beset by multiple enemies, they sweep their
weapon around them, scattering ropes of blood
and severed limbs from their opponents. Crung
always fight to the death and pursue fleeing
enemies, though not more than a few yards outside
of the Occlusion.

originalText:
Hood

About fifty years ago, reports in cities all across the
Empire and Confederacy began filtering into the
watch headquarters and constable offices of strange
dwarfs moving through the city under the cover of
night, bound on inscrutable errands, but sometimes
spotted near scenes where crimes had transpired.
Believing them to be criminals, these mysterious
agents gained the hood moniker and it has stayed
with them. And since they first began moving into
civilized lands, these figures have gained a sinister
reputation, for no one has, of yet, discerned from
where they have come or what they’re after.
Dwarf Thralls: A band of dwarfs, thinking to win
fame and fortune by plundering the Occlusion, spent
a decade digging a long tunnel into the underbelly
of this diabolical fortress. When they finally
broke through the subterranean walls, they found
themselves overwhelmed by the monstrous denizens
crawling about in the depths. Rather than butcher the
intruders, these creatures captured them and dragged
them to the cabalists as a gift.

--- PDF p. 13 ---
HOOD

DIFFICULTY 25

Size 1/2 monster
Perception 15 (+5); darksight
Defense 15 (hard leather); Health 30; Insanity —; Corruption 4
Strength 11 (+1), Agility 13 (+3), Intellect 11 (+1), Will 12 (+2)
Speed 10

ATTACK OPTIONS
Long Knife (melee) +3 with 2 boons (2d6)
Dagger (melee or short range) +3 with 2 boons (1d6)
Hand Crossbow (medium range) +3 with 2 boons
(1d6 plus Shadow Poison)
Shadow Poison If the target is a creature, it must get a
success on a Strength challenge roll or become poisoned
for 1 minute. While poisoned in this way, the target is
also blinded. If the target is already poisoned, it takes
3d6 extra damage.

SPECIAL ACTIONS
Hide in Shadows The hood can attempt to hide when it is
in an area at least partially obscured by shadows, even if
it is being observed.
Shadow Step When the hood is in an area obscured by
shadows or darkness, it can use an action, or a triggered
action on its turn, to teleport to an open space within
medium range that is also obscured by shadows or
darkness.

MAGIC
Power 1
Shadow nightfall blade (2), darkness (1), shadow dart (1)

The cabalists had begun to extract strange lampreylike creatures through tiny portals torn open to the edges
of the universe. The creatures showed intelligence and
a capacity for working magic, but they could not find a
way to communicate with them. The gift of thirty dwarf
prisoners, offered them a possible solution.
The cabalists drained the hoods of their vital fluids
and removed the backs of their heads, including
their brains. They then pumped the bodies with an
alchemical fluid and attached a glass container, filled
with the same fluid and the weird parasites, to their
heads. This new arrangement allowed the parasites
to control the bodies and reveal their secrets to their
summoners, speaking in High Archaic.
Alien Intellect: The entities, called ageet, drawn
from the edges of the universe, were spawned from
the heaving bulk of a dead god set adrift in the darkest
reaches of space. Each ageet possesses a fragment
of the being’s intellect and command over darkness.
They are keenly interested in their adopted world
and have become willing accomplices in the Cabal’s
insidious work. Ageet consider themselves partners
with the Cabal, rather than their servants. One day,
they might grow powerful enough to branch out on
their own and pursue their own agenda.

Murderous Spies

Hoods undertake missions involving intelligence
gathering, sabotage, murder, and mayhem. They
use Shadow magic to cover their movements and to
enter places normally forbidden to them. The Cabal

chooses targets, using numerological formulas to
predict which individuals and places might frustrate
their efforts to prepare the world for the coming
darkness and the hoods carry out the task without
hesitation or complaint. When on missions, hoods
work in small numbers, no more than three. If they
need additional muscle, they recruit cultists from the
field and consider them expendable.

originalText:
Megpee

The Cabal of the Black Sun has eyes and ears
everywhere, trusting the work of gathering
information to the megpees, who ensure that other
agents in the field carry out their missions. These
strange bird constructs have the bodies of ravens with
the heads of porcelain dolls, whose black eyes swivel
in their heads and who speak without ever moving
their cold lips. Megpees accompany hoods and
cultists at work, recording everything they witness so
they can give a full accounting to their masters when
they wing their way back to the Occlusion. When not
on a mission, the megpees sometimes gather in flocks
atop the battlements or wheel in the sky overhead,
diving at travelers to get a good look at those who will
soon grace the dungeon depths below the Occlusion.

13

--- PDF p. 14 ---
MEGPEE

DIFFICULTY 10

Size 1/8 construct
Perception 14 (+4); darksight
Defense 14; Health 6; Insanity —; Corruption —
Strength 6 (–4), Agility 14 (+4), Intellect 12 (+2), Will 11 (+1)
Speed 16; flier (swoop)
Immune damage from disease and poison; asleep,
charmed, diseased, fatigued, frightened, poisoned

ATTACK OPTIONS
Talons (melee) +4 with 1 boon (1d6)

SPECIAL ATTACKS
Compelling Direction The megpee uses an action, or a
triggered action on its turn, to reach into the mind of
one creature it can see within long range and makes
an Intellect attack roll against the target’s Will. On a
success, the megpee moves the target up to half its
Speed in a manner it can normally move. The movement
does not trigger free attacks.
Destructive Chime The megpee makes a chiming noise
that causes a wave of force to spread out from a point
in its space out to a 5-yard radius. Each creature in
the area other than the megpee must make a Strength
challenge roll with 1 bane. A creature takes 5d6 damage
and becomes stunned for 1 round on a failure, or just
takes half the damage on a success. Once the megpee
uses Destructive Chime, it must wait 1 minute before it
can use it again.

14

Messengers of the Black Sun
The disciples sometimes dispatch a megpee to treat
with a particularly difficult and dangerous adversary.
The megpee is empowered to bargain on behalf of the
Cabal, though within limits, and so in this capacity,
the megpee might make all kinds of offers in order to
tempt their foes from continuing their efforts against
the Cabal. Clever, megpees conduct these meetings
from a distance, usually perched somewhere they can
be heard but out of their opponent’s reach.

originalText:
Scran

Tunnels riddle the ground beneath the Occlusion.
These lightless corridors collect the filth and offal
that drain from the encrusted chutes and pipes
that carry the effluvia from the crooked chambers
above. Where these jagged tubes jut from the walls,
those wandering the depths are bound to find scran
suckling upon them, engorging themselves of the foul
nectar spawned from the countless horrors infesting
this blight on the world.
Scran are among the rare few monsters
created by the Cabal that have managed
to perpetuate themselves and thus
escape from the Occlusion to ensconce
themselves elsewhere in the Patchwork
Lands. Scran have bodies of worms, their
rubbery flesh maggot-white and bristling
with keratin horns. Human heads with
slick faces contorted into grimaces of
pain and horror extend out from the
front of their bodies, while their tails
terminate in puckered sphincters from
which issues a sweet-smelling, thin,
yellowish slime.
Although bred from humans, they
retain none of the higher thought or
intelligence of their ancestors. Instead,
the fulfilment of their basic needs defines
their existence. They slither through the
noisome dark in search of food, water,
and suitable mates. Some gather into
colonies of modest size, though such
gatherings typically serve to protect a
clutch of eggs, each a black, hard shell
encasing a noxious stew and embryo.
Scran moan, chuff, and make other
noises, but they never speak.

--- PDF p. 15 ---
SCRAN

DIFFICULTY 1

originalText:
TATTERDEMALION

DIFFICULTY 1

Size 1 frightening monster

Size 1/2 construct

Perception 10 (+0); darksight
Defense 9; Health 11; Insanity —; Corruption 1d3
Strength 11 (+1), Agility 9 (–1), Intellect 4 (–6), Will 11 (+1)
Speed 8
Immune frightened, prone
Void the Bowels When a scran dies, it pushes its internal
organs out through its anus in a river of yellowish slime.
Each creature within 1 yard of the scran must get a
success on an Agility challenge roll or be covered in
the stuff. The stench lingers for 1d6 days and imposes 1
bane on all of the creature’s Perception rolls. As well, a
creature coated in the filth can be smelled from up to
100 yards away.

Perception 10 (+0); darksight
Defense 9; Health 30; Insanity 1d6; Corruption 1d3 – 1
Strength 12 (+2), Agility 9 (–1), Intellect 8 (–2), Will 9 (–1)
Speed 8
Immune damage from disease and poison; diseased,
fatigued, poisoned
Sudden Viciousness When a tatterdemalion becomes
injured, it becomes vicious for 1 minute. While vicious,
the tatterdemalion makes attack rolls with 1 boon and its
attacks deal 1d6 extra damage.
Spirit Spawn When a tatterdemalion becomes
incapacitated, it dies. Roll a d6. On an odd number, a
manes forms in its space and takes the next available
turn. The manes is hostile to all creatures except spirits.
Craven When a creature attacks the tatterdemalion, the
tatterdemalion becomes frightened for 1 round.
Broken If a tatterdemalion takes damage while it’s not
injured, it takes 1d6 extra damage.

ATTACK OPTIONS
Teeth (melee) +1 with 1 boon (2d6 plus Attach)
Attach When a scran gets a success on an attack roll it
makes using its teeth against a creature of flesh and
blood, it can use a triggered action to clamp down
on the target and remains so for as long as the scran
concentrates. Whenever the scran uses an action to
concentrate on this effect, the target to which it is
attached takes 2d6 damage. If a target has a number
of attached scran equal to 1 + its Size or more, the
target falls prone and cannot crawl or stand up until the
number of attached scran are fewer than this number.
A creature that can reach a creature with one or
more attached scran can use an action to pull the scran
from the creature. The creature must make a Strength
challenge roll. The creature removes the scran with a
success. Whether the roll results in a success or failure,
the creature to which the scran was attached takes 1d6
damage from having its body torn by the scran’s teeth.

Maggot Infestation
The Cabal has never taken an interest in the scran and
their lack of action permits the scran to move freely
below the Occlusion and, in some case, away from the
Cabal’s area of influence. In recent years, many of the
petty rulers of the Patchwork Lands have complained
of scran infestations growing beneath their ramshackle
castles and keeps. Most of these minor rulers have
turned to mercenaries and adventurers to clear out the
infestation lest their numbers grow out of control. Scran
lay dozens of eggs, which hatch in a matter of days.

Tatterdemalion

Maintaining the Occlusion falls to a wretched breed
of constructs assembled from discarded body parts
and other materials and to which the disciples bind
the spirits of their enemies, starting with the students
they murdered in Lij. Tatterdemalions appear as
misshapen dwarfs, all twisted up and broken, and
they cover themselves in whatever scraps of material
they can find. They cringe away from threatening
creatures, but can muster up courage when cornered,
becoming vicious fighters. Even though the spirits
bound to them are unwilling victims of the Cabal’s
magic, each has been imbued with an overriding
sense of self-preservation to prevent them from
simply committing suicide.

ATTACK OPTIONS
Improvised Weapon (melee) +2 with 1 bane (1d3)

END OF THE ROUND
Flee! If the tatterdemalion is frightened, it moves up to
half its Speed away from the source of its fear without
triggering free attacks.

Tatterdemalions speak haltingly in the Common
Tongue, frequently misusing words, revealing the
disorder of their minds.

Unlikely Ally

Freeing a spirit from a tatterdemalion could give the
player characters a useful ally, provided they can
somehow communicate with it and convince it to aid
them in their fight against the Cabal. These spirits
have no reason to love their tormentors and so might
divulge certain secrets that would be of use to those
who would end their dark tyranny.

Black Sun Disciples

The Black Sun Manuscript’s reputation lures the mad
and the wicked into scouring the lands for it, to
uncover this most unholy tome and learn its secrets.
The Cabal of the Black Sun quietly encourages
outsiders to seek out the book and even circulates
forgeries containing a few tantalizing truths to draw
these outsiders into their fold and make them witting
or unwitting servants of the Cabal’s designs. As their
numbers grow and spread, so too does the Cabal’s
network of minions.
A typical cult of the Black Sun grows up around
one or two leaders who have come into possession
of fragments from the book, a copy, or one of the
forgeries. Upon studying the writings, the leaders
come to see Rathran Crux as their prophet and
guide. Some cults even go so far as to worship him,
offering prayers and sacrifices to his name. The
leaders gather likeminded individuals, preying on
the weak and the fragile and drawing them in with

15

--- PDF p. 16 ---
promises of vengeance, power, or whatever else they
could desire. These cultists never learn the full truth
of what their leaders have discovered—which is in
itself little compared to the knowledge amassed by
the Cabalists—to ensure these disciples never balk
at the Black Sun’s ultimate aim and betray them to
their enemies.
Black Sun disciples pursue their own agendas.
They study dark magic, seek out relics left behind
by the Men of Gog, and kidnap innocents for ritual
sacrifices in the hopes of gaining the Black Sun’s
attention. Disciples who have shown themselves to
be resourceful and competent might earn attention
from a megpee, who then makes use of them for
its masters. These disciples accompany hoods on
missions or might be sacrificed as a distraction while
other agents move in to secure objects that the Cabal
would have for themselves.
Like the Cabalists, self-mutilation preoccupies
cult members and most sport signs of their debased
interests. When gathering for unholy ceremonies,
they don gray robes with pointed hoods that conceal
all but their eyes, over which is painted the black sun.

BLACK SUN DISCIPLE

DIFFICULTY 1

Size 1 human
Perception 9 (–1)
Defense 11; Health 17; Insanity 1d3; Corruption 1d3
Strength 12 (+2), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 9 (–1), Will 8 (–2)
Speed 10
Relentless When a Black Sun disciple would become
incapacitated, roll a d6. On an even number, it
immediately heals 1d6 damage and loses this trait
until it completes a rest.

ATTACK OPTIONS
Sword (melee) +2 with 1 boon (1d6 + 2)

SPECIAL ACTIONS
Horrid Sacrifice The Black Sun disciple can use an action to
harm itself, taking 1d6 + 2 damage. If a Black Sun disciple
leader is within short range of the disciple, the leader
can either regain an expended casting or use a triggered
action to cast a spell.

Treasures of the Cabal

In addition to sculpting creatures and reaching
across vast distances to pluck alien entities from the
furthest reaches of the universe, the Cabalists have
also created many strange devices to aid them in
their work. Although these items most likely reside
in the Occlusion, some might have found their way
elsewhere, likely corrupting whomever happens to
find them.
The Cabalists often create magical objects in
order to help them in their work, but many times
their efforts fail and result in oddities with strange
properties. Enchanted objects originating with the
Cabal are made from metal, usually bronze, fashioned
to look like horns, teeth, organs, and other organic
body parts, or collections of those parts. Others
resemble machines with clockwork components,
hoses, flashing lights, and other mechanical
components.
When rolling to determine the enchanted object’s
properties, you can use the tables presented in
Shadow (see page 208) or you can use the following
table instead.
